rgb_path: The original colour clip. SAM 3 usually segments on this, and it is the only way to catch an object the depth map missed. Picking a clip fills the depth box automatically when <clip>_depth.mp4 can be found. You can also drop a video here.
depth_path: The DepthCrafter depth map to edit (<clip>_depth.mp4). It is never overwritten: the edit is written to the output folder.
load_clip: Read both videos into memory for editing. If an edit of this clip was saved before in the output folder, it is reopened.
import_depthcrafter: Browse the clips of the most recent DepthCrafter job. The matching depth map is filled in for you.
view: RGB shows the colour clip, Depth the original depth map, Edited the depth map with every enabled layer applied. Brighter is nearer.
overlay: Tint each layer's mask in its colour. The selected layer is drawn stronger and outlined.
colormap: Show depth in colour instead of grey. Small steps in depth are much easier to see: the colour comes from the map's full 10 bits, so even a single level of difference changes it.
tool: What a click on the picture does. Add: mark part of an object (Ctrl+click starts another object). Remove: cut an area out of the mask. Box: drag around an object. Gradient: drag from the near end of the object to its far end. Right-click always removes. Shape: draw a mask that holds on every frame, for a locked-off shot -- nothing to track (pick Points, Rectangle or Ellipse beside the tool).
layers: Each layer is one selection -- one or more objects -- and the depth edit applied inside it. Layers apply bottom to top, so a lower layer's edit is what the one above it sees.
layer_new: Start an empty layer. Clicking the picture with no layer selected starts one too.
layer_delete: Remove the selected layer, its prompts and its masks.
layer_move: Change the order layers are applied in.
layer_enabled: Switch this layer's edit off without losing it.
install_packages: Install the four packages SAM 3 needs (timm, iopath, scipy, pycocotools) into this StereoCrafter environment with uv. You see the list of changes and confirm before anything happens; nothing is removed.
download_weights: Download SAM 3's weights (about 3.4 GB) into weights/SAM3. Meta gates them: request access on huggingface.co/facebook/sam3 first and log in on this machine with `hf auth login`.
unload_model: Free SAM 3's VRAM now. It loads again on the next click. Studio also frees it when another tab needs the GPU.
offload_frames: Keep the clip's frames, and the memory SAM 3 builds up frame by frame as it tracks, in system RAM instead of on the GPU. Without it a long clip needs about 6 MB of VRAM a frame for the frames alone, and the tracking memory grows with every frame and every object. A little slower; leave it on for long scenes or several objects.
segment_on: Which picture SAM 3 looks at for this layer. RGB is the usual choice and the only way to catch something the depth map missed. Depth is for shapes that are clear in depth but busy in colour.
text_prompt: Name what to select -- 'person', 'car', 'road', 'tree trunk' -- and SAM 3 finds every instance on this frame. A layer with only a name also picks up new instances that enter later while tracking. Once you add or remove with clicks, the layer tracks the instances found on this frame, with your clicks applied.
track: Follow this layer's objects through every frame of the clip, forwards and backwards from where you prompted. Needed before the edit applies to the whole clip. If the mask drifts, step to a frame where it is wrong, fix it there with Add/Remove clicks and track again: SAM 3 uses every frame you corrected, not just the first.
clear_prompts: Forget this layer's clicks, boxes and text, and its masks. The edit settings are kept.
brightness: Move the object nearer (+) or further (-), as a share of the clip's full depth range.
contrast: Stretch (above 1x) or squash (below 1x) the depth differences inside the object, about its own middle depth. 0x makes it perfectly flat. In Add: the gradient's depth differences.
flatten: Pull the object towards a single depth -- its middle depth -- without moving it. Good for screens, signs and walls that should be flat. In Add: pulls a gradient towards flat.
smooth: Blur the depth inside the object only, to remove noise without softening its edge against the background. In Add: smooths a gradient.
opacity: How strongly the whole edit applies. 50% is halfway between the original and the edit.
edge_snap: Pull the mask's edge onto the depth map's own edges, within this many pixels. SAM's masks are drawn at a lower resolution and follow colour edges; the edit belongs exactly where the depth changes. 0 turns it off. The Masks overlay shows the snapped edge.
edge_top: Move only the object's TOP edge, in pixels of the depth map; the bottom edge stays where it is. Negative pulls the top in (the depth behind shows there) -- like a negative Y dilation on just this object's top, e.g. a beam bent upward by Y dilation in Splatting. Positive pushes it out.
edge_bottom: Move only the object's BOTTOM edge, in pixels of the depth map; the top edge stays where it is. Negative pulls the bottom in (the depth behind shows there); positive pushes it out.
edge_left: Move only the object's LEFT edge; the right edge stays where it is. Negative pulls the left side in (the depth behind shows there) -- like a negative X dilation on just this object's left; positive pushes it out. Useful where an object's depth spills past its outline on one side.
edge_right: Move only the object's RIGHT edge; the left edge stays where it is. Negative pulls the right side in (the depth behind shows there); positive pushes it out.
grow: Expand (+) or shrink (-) the mask before editing, in pixels of the depth map. This only changes WHICH pixels the layer's edits apply to -- it does not move the depth itself (to move the object's depth edge, use Top edge / Bottom edge). Grow a little to cover a halo of wrong depth around an object; shrink to keep the edit off the background.
feather: Soften the mask's edge so the edit fades in over this many pixels instead of stopping at a hard line.
fill_holes: Fill gaps inside the mask, e.g. between a person's arm and body when SAM 3 left them out.
frame_range: In: the layer starts at the current frame. Out: it stops at the current frame. All: every frame.
gradient_enabled: Replace the depth inside the mask with a ramp from a near value to a far value. For objects that recede into the distance -- a road, a floor, a long wall, a table seen at an angle -- which a depth model often flattens.
gradient_shape: Linear ramps along the line you draw. Radial ramps outward from its near end, for round objects.
gradient_blend: Replace: the ramp is the new depth. Only nearer / Only further: the ramp can only pull pixels one way, leaving anything already correct. Add: the ramp tilts the existing depth instead of replacing it.
gradient_near: Depth at the near end of the line (the end you started dragging from). 100% is the nearest depth in the clip.
gradient_far: Depth at the far end of the line. 0% is the furthest depth in the clip.
gradient_curve: 1x is a straight ramp. Above 1x the depth stays near for longer and falls away late; below 1x it falls away early.
gradient_detail: How much of the object's own surface detail rides on top of the ramp. 0% is a perfectly smooth ramp.
gradient_follow: Pin the ramp to the object's bounding box, so it moves and scales with the object. Off: the ramp stays fixed in the frame.
gradient_sample: Set Near and Far from the object's own nearest and furthest depth on this frame -- a good starting point for keeping its overall depth while fixing its shape.
global_invert: Swap near and far for the whole map, for depth maps that use the opposite convention (dark = near).
global_levels: Stretch the depth range: whatever is at the far point becomes the furthest depth, whatever is at the near point the nearest. Applied to the whole frame before any layer.
global_gamma: Above 1x brings the middle depths nearer; below 1x pushes them away. The ends stay put.
global_contrast: Stretch or squash depth differences across the whole frame, about the middle.
global_brightness: Move the whole frame nearer or further.
output_dir: Where the edited map is written, as <clip>_depth.mp4 -- the name Splatting expects -- together with the project files that let you reopen the edit. Defaults to an 'edited' folder beside the depth maps.
send_to_splatting: After a render, Splatting's import button fills in this clip and the edited map instead of the original DepthCrafter output.
save_project: Save layers, prompts, masks and settings without rendering. Rendering saves them too.
render: Write the edited depth map. Lossless 10-bit HEVC in the same format DepthCrafter writes, so every pixel no layer touched is exactly as it was. With Render at source resolution on, it is written at the source video's size instead.
despeck_on: Despeck (in Alter): DepthCrafter's bright specks and soft glows just inside the LEFT edges in the mask come down to the object's own depth beside them -- the level each is lowered to is taken from the pixels beside it on every frame, so the mask only has to be tracked. Works with the rest of Alter (it goes first). Off, the specks are back as they were (cyan under Specks), to compare.
despeck_strength: Strength: how far the specks in this layer come down. 100% lowers each all the way to the object's own depth beside it; less, part of the way -- for a thing whose left side really is a little nearer, like a face turned three-quarters.
level_edge: Level to edge (in Alter): for a small thing -- a floating particle -- whose white dot sits inside a grey body, with nothing beside it for Despeck to go by. Anything in the mask brighter than the grey around its outer edge comes down to that grey, on every frame (the edge is measured afresh on each). A particle that really is near is white all the way to its edge, so it stays as it is. Mask the particle snugly: an edge that reaches the background reads darker. Strength is how far.
global_despeck: Despeck the whole frame: Alter's Despeck on every left edge in the frame, no layer needed -- DepthCrafter's bright specks and soft glows there come down to the depth of the object beside them, on every frame. It goes first, before Invert and the rest. Watch the whole shot with Specks on: something whose left side really is nearer (a face turned three-quarters) can lose a little -- lower Strength, or leave this off and use Despeck in a layer for just that object. Takes about a tenth of a second a frame more, on a graphics card.
global_match:
Local Match: for a shot where the camera doesn't move. Sometimes DepthCrafter changes its mind part-way through about how far one part of a still scene is -- a hedge grey at the start and black at the end, so in 3D it slowly pushes in or out though nothing moved. Local Match makes every frame's depth agree, area by area, with the one frame you pick (Use This Frame), while keeping each frame's fine detail. Pick a frame that looks the way you want the whole shot to look.

Anything that moves is left as it is: outlines that shifted (a turned head, an arm) don't count, so nothing gets a glow around it, and a frame where something comes right up to the lens (a person walking past) is skipped entirely.

Not for pans, dollies or zooms: when the camera moves, everything in the frame changes, and Local Match would drag it all back toward the picked frame. It goes first, before Despeck, Invert and the rest. Off by default.
global_match_frame: Use This Frame: makes the frame showing now the one every frame is matched to. Scrub to a frame that looks right -- here, one where the far parts of the scene are as dark as you want them -- and press it. The frame number shows beside the button. Undo puts the previous one back.
global_match_strength: Strength: how far each frame is moved toward the picked frame. 100% matches it fully; lower it to only lessen the drift, keeping a little of DepthCrafter's own change.
global_despeck_threshold: Threshold: how far something must stand above the object beside it before the whole-frame Despeck takes it, as a share of the depth range. 0 takes everything it finds; raise it when it changes something that was fine -- a lamp's or a rounded thing's gently brighter left side -- and only the clear specks are taken. Below half of it nothing is taken, from it up all of it, eased between. Watch with Specks on: what it leaves isn't tinted.
global_despeck_reach: Reach: how far in from a left edge the whole-frame Despeck works, as a share of the frame's width (2% by default). Lower it when it flattens the gentle shading on the left of a rounded thing; raise it for a glow that runs further in.
global_despeck_step: Edge: how sharp a drop to the left counts as an object's left edge, as a share of the depth range (4% by default). Raise it to leave the small steps inside an object alone -- one part overlapping another -- and keep to edges against what is far behind.
global_despeck_zone: Left / Right / Top / Bottom: where the whole-frame Despeck works, as shares of the frame -- outside the box it leaves the map alone (it eases in over about 1% at each line, so no seam shows). Drawn on the picture while this page is open. For a shot where nothing needs it above a head or past a table, keep it to where the specks are; under Specks, those outside show cyan.
global_despeck_strength: Strength: how far the specks in the whole frame come down. 100% all the way to the object's own depth beside them; less, part of the way.
specks: Highlight Specks: tints the bright specks and glows DepthCrafter leaves just inside the LEFT edges of things, on this frame, by how far a Despeck layer would lower them -- cyan where no Despeck layer covers them yet, orange where one does. Turn on Despeck in the layer over the cyan ones (Alter) and watch them turn orange as you step through the clip. Only the picture changes.
layer_mode: Alter: the mask selects, and the settings change the depth already there. Add: the mask IS the shape -- inside it the depth is replaced by Depth (Push / pull and the gradient on top), for an object the depth map missed or left as a blob. Add skips Edge snap: the outline is the point. The other controls work in Add too: the edge moves move the shape's own edges, and Smooth, Contrast and Flatten shape a gradient's depth. Erase: the object is taken out -- its depth is filled from the depth around it here, and Erase from Clip removes it from the clip itself with ROSE.
add_depth: Add's depth, 0-100% (100% nearest). Sample takes it from the object on the frame showing.
add_depth_sample: Set Depth from the object on the frame showing: the nearest part of what the depth map has under the mask.
render_hires: Render the edited depth map at the source video's size (1920 wide for a 1080p clip) instead of the depth map's. RGB layers use SAM 3's full-size masks, so an object's real outline reaches Splatting -- as Detect Text's does -- instead of the depth map's coarse pixels. Larger file, slower render; off writes at the depth map's own size.
upscale_map: Re-read this clip's depth map enlarged to the source video's size (1920 wide for a 1080p clip), so every edit -- masks, Edge snap, the edge dials, Grow, Feather -- works in the clip's own pixels instead of the depth map's coarser ones, and the Depth and Edited views show exactly what will be rendered. The map is enlarged the way Splatting enlarges it, so anything you don't edit splats exactly as before. Your layers stay: RGB layers use SAM 3's full-size masks; other layers' masks are enlarged (Start Tracking again for a finer outline). Costs memory (about 3 GB for 750 frames of 1080p) and makes each preview frame slower. Load Clip goes back to the map's own size.
key_static: A static key on this frame for this layer: its number settings (Depth, Push / pull, Opacity, Feather, Grow, the gradient's ends...) as they are now. From here they hold until the next key. Shortcut S.
key_dynamic: A dynamic key on this frame for this layer: from the key before it, the settings slide smoothly to these values by this frame -- a depth that follows an object moving nearer, say. Shortcut D. The choices (Alter / Add, Fill holes, the gradient's shape) and the frame range aren't keyed.
erase_from_clip: Takes every enabled Erase layer's object out of the clip itself with ROSE (it also removes the object's shadow, reflection or glow). Only the frames with something to erase are processed, at about 480p; ROSE's result replaces the clip inside the mask only, every other pixel stays the original. The clip is replaced in place, so Splatting and DepthCrafter use the erased one; the original is kept in edit_history beside it, with the erase mask. Slow: minutes per 81 frames. Track the objects through the clip first.
rose_setup: ROSE runs in its own environment in weights/ROSE (it needs older libraries than Studio's). Setting it up clones ROSE, builds that environment and downloads about 3.7 GB of weights. Needs git and uv.
steady: Steady a tracked mask over this many frames either side: each pixel is in the mask when at least half the masks around it have it, so an outline that SAM 3 draws a little differently every frame -- an edge with nothing strong to hold on to -- stops shimmering. Best on a locked-off shot or a slow object; on fast movement keep it low, or the mask lags a little behind. Off (0) uses each frame's mask as tracked.
close_gaps: Seal tears and notches in the mask up to about twice this wide -- gaps that reach the mask's edge, which Fill holes can't close (it only fills holes the mask surrounds). The outline elsewhere stays where it is.
erase_steps: ROSE's denoising steps. Fewer is faster (time is roughly in proportion) and softer; 50 is ROSE's own. Try 20-30 to judge a mask quickly.
erase_seed: The random start ROSE's fill grows from. The same seed and settings give the same result; another seed gives another fill to compare.
erase_grow: How far past the object, in the clip's pixels, ROSE repaints. A little room (12 at 1920 wide) takes the object's soft edge and its fringe with it; more reaches a shadow or glow the mask missed, but repaints more of what should stay.
erase_feather: How softly ROSE's result blends back into the original at the edge of the repainted area, in the clip's pixels.
erase_size: The resolution ROSE works at, in the clip's shape: 480p is about what it was trained at. 576p / 720p are sharper but slower, need more VRAM, and are past what it was trained on -- compare before trusting them. Only the repainted area comes from ROSE either way.
erase_window: Frames ROSE takes in one pass. 81 is its base model's length and keeps the fill steadiest over time; shorter passes need less VRAM (for a smaller card), cross-faded where they meet.
putback: Put the erased object back in the finished 3D, at a depth of its own: Merging lays it over both eyes. The clip stays erased for DepthCrafter, Splatting and Inpainting, so the scene behind keeps its depth. For glass, a rainy window, a sign or a pole that should sit at its own depth.
putback_mode: Add: what erasing took away (the original minus the erased clip) is added back -- for glass, reflections, rain, smoke: anything seen through. Over: the original's pixels inside the object's own outline are laid over -- for a solid object.
putback_parallax: Where it sits, as Splatting's shift in percent of the picture's width: 0 = the screen plane (both eyes the same), + in front of the screen, - behind it. Sample sets it from the object's own depth.
putback_sample: A parallax for every frame: the depth map's median under the Erase layers on that frame (before erasing), times the depth factor, through the clip's Splatting sidecar -- so it follows the surface when the camera or the object moves. Typing a parallax instead uses that one on every frame.
erase_method: ROSE: an object comes out of the clip (and its shadow, reflection, glow), its place filled in by ROSE -- for a sign, a pole, a logo, a mark. Static: reflections that hold still on glass come off -- for a locked-off shot where the camera and the lights don't move but what is seen through the glass does (a TV screen, a shop window); no model, seconds, no GPU. Dust: dust and specks on glass the camera rides with (a windshield seen from inside a car) come off -- they hold still on screen while the world moves behind -- for Put Back to lay on the glass (Add, Glass Plane); each frame's own dust, so all of it moves. Either way Put back can lay what came off at a depth of its own.
erase_static_size: The widest reflection shape kept, in the clip's pixels (31 suits lamp reflections in a 1920-wide clip). A shape wider than this, or one that isn't bright on every frame, stays in the clip.
putback_factor: Sample's depth factor: the depth under the mask on each frame times this. x1.0 puts it on the surface (a mark, dirt, rain on the glass); x0.5 puts it inside, about twice as far away -- where a mirror image sits (a reflection in a screen or a window). Press Sample after changing it.
erase_prefill:
Fills the object's area from around it before ROSE erases. ROSE normally sees the object under the mask, so it can take the object's shadows and reflections with it. But a big object (a person filling a close-up) can come back redrawn instead of removed. Pre-filled, ROSE has nothing to redraw and invents what's behind it.

Auto: on when the object covers 10% of the frame or more. On / Off: always / never. Off keeps ROSE's shadow and reflection removal for small objects.
erase_refine:
A second ROSE pass at the clip's own size, in tiles (832x560, ROSE's own size; 3x2 at 1080p; only the tiles with something to erase), over the first pass's result. Sharper -- the first pass works shrunk to the Size above -- with the colour kept from the first pass, since the tiles each drift a little in tone.

About as long again as the first pass, or longer. Worth it for a big object at a high resolution.
shape_kind: The shape to draw, for static camera shots (a layer drawn, not tracked: its shapes are its mask on every frame). Points: click each corner of any outline -- click the first point again, double-click, or press Enter to close it; right-click or Backspace takes the last point back, Esc drops it. Rectangle / Ellipse: drag one out. Hold Ctrl as you start a shape to cut its area out of the layer instead. A shape drawn while a tracked layer is selected starts a layer of its own, so tracking never wipes it.
erase_dust_size: The widest speck taken as dust, in the clip's pixels (9 suits dust on a windshield in a 1920-wide clip). Wider shapes -- the glass's own edges, a reflection -- stay in the clip.
